summary: A survey of giants and titans in world folklore, covering Greek titans, Norse jötnar, biblical Nephilim and Anakim, Irish Fomorians, and giants in other cultures. It quotes scholars on what these beings symbolize and notes how modern media reimagines them as metaphors for human struggles. The piece concludes that giants endure because they embody humanity's fears and aspirations.
one_line: Overview of giants and titans across mythologies, from Greek titans and Norse jötnar to Fomorians, with scholar commentary and modern reinterpretations.
key_facts: Hesiod's "Theogony", around the 8th century BCE, introduces the Greek titans, a race of deities that preceded the Olympian gods.
The 12 original titans were born of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky) and included Cronus, Rhea, Oceanus, and Hyperion.
The titans fell in the Titanomachy, a divine war in which the Olympians, led by Zeus, overthrew them.

Professor Thalia Kountouris of the University of Athens said titans were personifications of earth, sea, sky, and even time itself; her seminar on October 15, 2023 covered ancient pottery showing cosmic order in titan iconography.

Dr. Erik Lundqvist of the University of Uppsala published 'Beyond Size: The Cultural Role of Jötnar in Norse Lore' on November 2, 2023, arguing jötnar are not simply 'giants' but beings of strength and elemental force.
The jötnar inhabited Jotunheim, one of the nine worlds connected by the cosmic tree Yggdrasil.
Ymir was the primeval jötunn from whom the world was created in Norse mythos; frost giants were adversaries of the gods.

Professor Abraham Levinsky of the Jerusalem Theological Seminary argues the Nephilim (Genesis 6:4) and Anakim (Numbers 13:33) are vestiges of giant lore; he spoke at a symposium on September 20, 2023.
The Nephilim are described as "heroes of old, men of renown" and their origins remain mysterious.
The Fomorians of Irish mythology were monstrous adversarial gods who battled the Tuatha Dé Danann; Dr. Fiona Byrne of University College Dublin says they embody chaos, darkness, and the untamed sea.
On October 31, 2023, Dr. Fiona Byrne presented findings from excavations in County Sligo with carvings that may represent the Fomorians.
Other giants include Sasquatch, the Gente Grande in Aztec codices, Hindu Rakshasas, and Japan's Daidarabotchi.
James McAllister's book "Colossus Reimagined: Giants and Titans in the 21st Century" argues modern giants are metaphors for human struggles, societal upheaval, or natural disasters.
Dr. Linda Zhang, an anthropologist at Harvard University, says giants bring our fantasies to scale and confront us with the limits of our existence.
